Quick Read

Trump Media and Rumble each fell 3% after September CPI came in at 3.7%, punishing loss-making, sentiment-driven stocks far harder than broader markets.

SPY dropped just 0.4% while Reddit's profitable ad-supported model gives it stronger footing than loss-making peers when rate expectations tighten.

Trump Media's next catalyst is SEC approval of its all-stock TAE Technologies merger, while its $1.7M quarterly revenue sits against a $238M net loss.

Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and Reddit didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat RDDT. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.

Speculative social-media stocks are falling faster than benchmark funds after a hotter-than-expected inflation report. Trump Media & Technology Group (NASDAQ:DJT) stock is trading at $7.38, down 5%. Meanwhile, Rumble (NASDAQ:RUM) stock is at $6.39, down 5% and matching the drop in Trump Media stock.

Alex Wong / Getty Images News via Getty Images

Benchmark funds are moving far less. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is down 0.64%. At the same time, the Global X Social Media ETF (NASDAQ:SOCL) is down 0.3%, a fraction of the drop in shares of the two aforementioned platforms.

Higher Inflation Reading Sends Speculative Names Lower

In September, the consumer price index (CPI) rose 3.7% from a year earlier, above the 3.6% Dow Jones consensus estimate. Stock index futures turned negative after the release. On a monthly basis, the index rose 0.6% from August, lifting it to its highest level in the past year.

A stronger inflation trend can push back the timing of Federal Reserve rate cuts, and that shift tends to weigh hardest on loss-making companies whose shares trade on sentiment. Long-term borrowing costs were already elevated, with the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.24% as of October 9. Both Trump Media and Rumble carry operating losses and lean on retail interest, which places them near the front of that revaluation.

3 Reasons We're Fans of Reddit (RDDT)

Reddit currently trades at $155.70 per share and has shown little upside over the past six months, posting a middling return of 0.8%. The stock also fell short of the S&P 500's 12% gain during that period.

Is now the time to buy RDDT? Or does the price properly account for its business quality and fundamentals? Find out in our full research report, it's free.

Why Is Reddit a Good Business?

Founded in 2005 by two University of Virginia roommates, Reddit (NYSE:RDDT) facilitates user-generated content across niche communities (called subreddits) that discuss anything from stocks to dating and memes.

1. Domestic Daily Active Visitors Skyrocket, Fueling Growth Opportunities

As a social network, Reddit generates revenue growth by increasing its user base and charging advertisers more for the ads each user is shown.

Over the last two years, Reddit's domestic daily active visitors, a key performance metric for the company, increased by 13.2% annually to 53.2 million in the latest quarter. This growth rate is strong for a consumer internet business and indicates people love using its offerings.

Reddit Domestic Daily Active Visitors
2. Eye-Popping Growth in Customer Spending

Average revenue per user (ARPU) is a critical metric to track because it measures how much the company earns from the ads shown to its users. ARPU can also be a proxy for how valuable advertisers find Reddit's audience and its ad-targeting capabilities.

Reddit's ARPU growth has been exceptional over the last two years, averaging 47.1%. Its ability to increase monetization while growing its domestic daily active visitors at an impressive rate reflects the strength of its platform, as its users are spending significantly more than last year.

Reddit ARPU
3. Excellent Free Cash Flow Margin Boosts Reinvestment Potential

If you've followed StockStory for a while, you know we emphasize free cash flow. Why, you ask? We believe that in the end, cash is king, and you can't use accounting profits to pay the bills.

Reddit has shown terrific cash profitability, driven by its lucrative business model that enables it to reinvest, return capital to investors, and stay ahead of the competition while maintaining an ample cushion. The company's free cash flow margin was among the best in the consumer internet sector, averaging an eye-popping 31.8% over the last two years.

Reddit Trailing 12-Month Free Cash Flow Margin
Final Judgment

These are just a few reasons why we think Reddit is one of the best consumer internet companies out there. With its shares lagging the market recently, the stock trades at 16.6× forward EV/EBITDA (or $155.70 per share). Is now a good time to initiate a position? title: AppLovin vs. Reddit: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
detail:
AppLovin vs. Reddit: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Jake Lerch, The Motley Fool
Tue, October 13, 2026 at 10:35 AM CDT 7 min read
APP
RDDT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Digital advertising is evolving rapidly as automation and community engagement take center stage. Choosing between AppLovin (NASDAQ:APP) and Reddit (NYSE:RDDT)requires examining how each captures value in this shifting landscape.

AppLovin provides the technical backbone for mobile app monetization, while Reddit operates a vast network of interest-based communities. Both companies have achieved profitability and exhibit rapid revenue growth, making them key candidates for investors evaluating high-growth platforms in the digital advertising space. Their distinct business models offer different ways to play the internet software market.

The case for AppLovin

AppLovin sells marketing software and advertising solutions to mobile app developers and consumer brands. Its platform includes tools like Axon Ads Manager for user acquisition, MAX for in-app bidding, and Adjust for analytics. In its latest annual report, filed for the period ending Dec. 31, 2024, the company stated it had 1,563 employees across 17 countries and highlighted its focus on advertising technology among tech stocks that support the global mobile economy. By divesting its apps business, the company now concentrates entirely on its software platform.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $5.5 billion, representing a significant 70% increase over the $3.2 billion reported in the previous year. The company reported net income of roughly $3.3 billion during this period, which is more than double its FY 2024 performance. This expansion yielded an impressive net margin of approximately 60.8%, demonstrating its ability to translate higher sales into earnings while maintaining low operating costs relative to its scale.

The company maintains a current ratio of about 3.3x, which indicates its ability to cover short-term liabilities with assets such as cash. As of its December 2025 balance sheet, its debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 1.7x, a measure of total debt relative to shareholders' equity. Free cash flow for the year reached close to $3.9 billion, representing cash from operations after subtracting capital expenditures. This strong cash generation provides the company with significant flexibility for future investments or debt reduction.

The case for Reddit

Reddit operates a community platform where users discuss interests across thousands of distinct forums, providing a unique environment for advertisers. It generates revenue primarily from third-party advertising, which accounted for approximately 94% of its revenue in FY 2025. While revenue is significantly concentrated among a small number of top advertisers, the company is now exploring additional streams, such as content licensing for artificial intelligence training and developer programs. This strategy aims to monetize the vast amount of user-generated content hosted on the site.

Reddit, Inc. (RDDT), headquartered in San Francisco, California, operates a digital community. Valued at $30.8 billion by market cap, the company offers a social networking platform where anyone can join a community to learn from one another, engage in authentic conversations, explore passions, research new hobbies, exchange goods and services, create new communities, and find belonging. The leading social media and content platform is expected to announce its fiscal third-quarter earnings for 2026 in the near term.

Ahead of the event, analysts expect Reddit to report a profit of $1.30 per share on a diluted basis, up 62.5% from $0.80 per share in the year-ago quarter. The company has consistently surpassed Wall Street's EPS estimates in its last four quarterly reports.

Reddit shares have faced pressure after investors worried that Alphabet Inc.'s (GOOGL) AI-generated summaries could replace traditional search links, threatening the platform's referral traffic and growth. This concern, highlighted by slowing domestic user growth and CEO Steve Huffman calling search referrals "choppy," overshadowed the company's strong Q2 earnings.

Analysts' consensus opinion on RDDT stock is reasonably bullish, with a "Moderate Buy" rating overall. Out of 32 analysts covering the stock, 19 advise a "Strong Buy" rating, one suggests a "Moderate Buy," 11 give a "Hold," and one recommends a "Strong Sell." RDDT's average analyst price target is $211.45, indicating a notable potential upside of 32.2% from the current levels.
